name: Tract Profile Computation
summary: Computes along-tract profiles of diffusion metrics (FA, MD, RD, AD) for a tractogram with DIPY, using optional centroid, medoid or skeleton reference curves, and outputs tractmeasures CSVs and profile plots.
description: Resamples each streamline to n_points nodes, orients them against a reference curve (QuickBundles/MBKM centroid or medoid, a tracklib density skeleton, or its nearest real streamline), samples the scalar maps along the nodes with optional distance weighting, and computes a dispersion measure. In the brainlife configuration it runs once per tensor metric (fa, md, ad, rd) and merges the results. Use it to compare microstructure along a bundle across subjects; the tractogram should contain a single bundle in the same space as the tensor maps.

inputs.description: Tractogram of a single white matter bundle (.tck).
inputs.requirements: Must be in the same space as the tensor maps and the reference T1.

inputs.description: Tensor (DTI) dataset; its FA, MD, AD and RD maps are profiled.
T1-weighted image used as spatial reference for loading .tck streamlines.

outputs.description: PNG plots of the tract profiles (and reference curve views).
Tractmeasures CSV with the profile of each metric at every node.

parameters.description: Number of nodes each streamline is resampled to along the tract.
Reference curve used to orient streamlines and weight nodes: none, QuickBundles centroid or medoid, tracklib density skeleton, or the real streamline nearest to the skeleton.
If true, weights each node's contribution by its distance to the reference curve (--weight-node-by-centroid).
Dispersion measure computed across streamlines at each node: std, cv, var or mad.
Matplotlib colormap used in the profile plots.
Percentile of the voxel density used to extract the skeleton backbone (skeleton methods).
If true, applies Gaussian smoothing to the voxel density map before skeleton extraction.
Minimum length fraction for a backbone segment to be kept (skeleton methods).
If true, hides the legend in the profile plots.

citations.text: Hayashi S, et al. brainlife.io: a decentralized and open-source cloud platform to support neuroscience research. Nat Methods 21(5):809-813 (2024).
